about: Attorney Kenneth F. Eichner, founder of The Eichner Law Firm , has a powerful legacy of courtroom victories. With more than 30 years of criminal law experience and over 160 jury trials, Mr. Eichner guides his clients to their best resolution, whether it is trial or a plea agreement. If clients think a case is headed to a jury trial, Eichner Law is considered the go-to firm. The firm's cases have appeared in every major news outlet.

Located in Denver, Colorado, Eichner Law represents clients charged in county, state or federal courts. As a former prosecutor, Mr. Eichner has succeeded in acquiring hundreds of dismissals, acquittals, or reduced sentences for clients facing a wide range of criminal charges, including assault , domestic violence , sexual assault , drug crimes , and white collar crimes and related civil actions, including fraud and securities violations and marijuana regulatory actions.

Mr. Eichner was listed in the Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Colorado in 2012 by the National Trial Lawyers and Avvo has given him its higest rating . He has been published in The Washington Post , The Huffington Post , and The Colorado Lawyer . He has also been featured on Denver's 9 News , and he has been a guest lecturer at Georgetown University Law School, the University of Colorado law school, and the University of Denver School of Law.

In 2019, Ken won the largest verdict in Colorado history for defamation and malicious prosecution : $2.7 million in Weld County, Colorado. During 2018 he represented a witness during Supreme Court Justice Kavanuagh’s congressional nomination hearing and subsequent FBI interview process. In 2017, Ken successfully blocked indictments relating to the Clinton email investigation and obtained dismissals of sexual assault charges against four individuals . These accomplishments led to his nomination for the Denver Bar Association’s Award of Merit, which recognizes attorneys for outstanding contributions and services rendered in the administration of justice.

Mr. Eichner graduated from Antioch School of Law in 1984, where he was an editor of the Law Review, and is licensed to practice in Colorado, Maryland, and Washington, D.C., in both state and federal courts.
